name: GOLDEN OYSTER

plan.note: share of the old 100-bag split; scaled to the 130-bag run, split not yet confirmed

blurb: FAST, WARM, PRETTY. THIN DATA IN THE SOURCES.

overview.v: Little detailed data exists. Pleurotus biology, differs from other oysters mainly in colour and temperature preference.
"A fast, warm one." Found growing wild in many places.
Golden primordia look coral-like on the blocks.
Invasive in places. Work on sporeless or low-spore strains is planned.
Top of the rack: seems to respond more to light. Often seen on the middle shelf of a mixed room.

cultivation.v: Does not survive cryo. Keep agar plugs in sterile water at about 1 °C.

cultivation.n: Textbook says treat like other oysters (F18-0159). That is not a measured figure.

timeline.v: 26.5 days (19-31), median of real picks. Wide spread.

climate.n: Pink, golden and phoenix temperatures are not in the sources.

climate.v: Responds more to light; give it the upper shelves.

yield_.n: Cap n Stem gives no figure.

yield_.v: 1.28 lb/block (1.32 in their efficiency table). Plan was 1.5 lb.
Yield up 39% and 6 days faster in warm months.

hazards.v: "Look pretty, but don't hold up in the pan." Old pinks and goldens smell bad in the bin.

hazards.n: No species-specific problems recorded. General oyster hazards (blotch, stroma) are in the BLUE OYSTER file.

notes.v: High Country Fungi (Avery) grows Cap n Stem house pink and gold strains. His "anti-cancer" claim for gold is unproven.
